Summary of what I learned and saved:

The error was a geometric-mean convention trap. The question asked for the "geometric mean of quarterly real GDP growth, **quarterly percent change at an annual rate**." I computed the geometric mean of the four annualized percent-change VALUES directly (→ 2.74). The gold answer (0.69) requires de-annualizing each rate to a per-quarter growth factor first:

  q_factor = (1 + R/100)^(1/4), geomean the factors, then ×100

A flat 2.74% annualized collapses to 0.68% per quarter, and the real 2017 quarters give 0.69. The key generalizable insight: **the year ranking is unaffected** by which convention you use (the transform is monotonic, so 2017 wins either way) — only the reported value differs. So a future agent should pick the year however, but always report the value via the de-annualization formula.
